title: Montréal
intro: One route to follow, with better meals, good desserts, and plenty of nearby discoveries. Pick one afternoon highlight; the rest stays easy.

hotel.name: Le Germain Montréal
hotel.label: Easy default
hotel.description: Refined, comfortable, and central. The cleanest shared-room choice.

booking: Default plan: Le Germain, Bota Bota on Saturday afternoon, and Monarque’s brasserie at 7 PM. Reserve those before going. Nothing is booked.
assumptions: Assumes driving from Boston and sharing one room with two beds. All times are Eastern. Recheck hours before leaving.

places.name: La Banquise
places.description: The flexible late-arrival poutine stop. Keep it casual tonight and save the nice meal for Saturday.
places.note: Check late kitchen hours before leaving the hotel.

places.name: St-Viateur Bagel
places.description: The original wood-fired bagel shop. Get a hot sesame bagel and watch the baking.
places.note: A quick start, not a sit-down brunch.

places.name: Café Olimpico
places.description: Espresso, an old-school café, and a lively neighborhood crowd.
places.note: Use the original Saint-Viateur location.

places.name: Bref
places.description: A bright gallery-boutique of ceramics, prints, and limited-edition design objects.
places.note: Saturday and Sunday 11 AM–5 PM on the contact page.

places.name: LVNEA
places.description: Locally made botanical perfumes: resins, woods, unusual atmospheric scents.
places.note: Entrance on Casgrain; published weekend hours 11 AM–6 PM.

places.name: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly
places.mapQuery: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly, 176 Rue Bernard Ouest
places.description: Art books, graphic novels, and good things to pick up and show each other.
places.note: On Bernard, by Bref and the record shops.

places.name: H Parfums
places.description: A polished niche-perfume boutique with independent houses to compare.
places.note: Saturday 10 AM–5 PM; Sunday noon–5 PM.

places.name: Schwartz’s Deli
places.description: Montréal smoked meat, mustard, and a pickle. Order medium-fat.
places.note: Use takeaway if the sit-down queue is long.

places.name: Habitat 67
places.description: A genuinely unusual stacked-housing experiment. A guided visit has more substance than a distant glance.
places.note: The 2026 tour calendar reaches Nov 22. Saturday slots are unverified; internal access requires a tour. Separate taxi trip across the water.

places.name: L’Express
places.description: A classic French bistro with a serious cellar and late service.
places.note: A dinner alternative to Monarque. Reserve by phone: +1 514 845-5333.

places.name: Cloakroom Bar
places.mapQuery: Cloakroom Bar, 2175 Rue de la Montagne
places.description: An intimate, no-menu cocktail bar that builds a drink around the flavors you like.
places.note: 25 seats, no reservations. Ask the price before ordering rare spirits.

places.name: Crew Collective & Café
places.description: Coffee under a spectacular former-bank ceiling. The interior is the attraction.
places.note: Go early to avoid the busiest tables.

places.name: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame
places.description: The blue-and-gold basilica interior is much more striking than a quick look at the façade.
places.note: Daytime adult entry starts at CAD 16 + tax; AURA starts at CAD 37 + tax. Sunday sightseeing is 12:30–4 PM.

places.name: L’Empreinte coopérative
places.description: Québec-made ceramics, glass, jewelry, and artisan objects in an actual makers’ cooperative.
places.note: 88 Saint-Paul Est. Confirm seasonal November opening times.

places.name: Rue Saint-Paul → Old Port
places.description: Stone streets, river views, little passages, and a long waterfront promenade.
places.note: The exposed river edge is windy; the streets are an easy shorter loop.

places.name: Olive et Gourmando
places.mapQuery: Olive et Gourmando, 351 Rue Saint-Paul Ouest
places.description: A cozy old-city café for excellent sandwiches, baked goods, and a proper lunch.
places.note: 351 Saint-Paul Ouest; published weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Takeaway avoids a brunch wait.

places.name: Leméac
places.description: A more polished Outremont bistro for a long lunch or proper dinner.
places.note: Weekend brunch/lunch 10 AM–3 PM; dinner 5–11 PM. Reserve.

places.name: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann
places.mapQuery: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann, 316 Avenue du Mont-Royal Est
places.description: A slice of caramelized, buttery kouign-amann. Split one while it is warm.
places.note: Saturday option. Tastet lists Sunday closed.

places.name: North Star Machines à Piastres
places.mapQuery: North Star Machines à Piastres, 3908 Boulevard Saint-Laurent
places.description: Vintage pinball, a drink, and a little friendly competition.
places.note: Opposite the Schwartz’s stretch; machine noise, not a quiet lounge. Confirm hours.

places.name: Bota Bota
places.description: Hot-and-cold baths on a floating spa, with river and city views. The strongest winter splurge.
places.note: Reserve a two-hour slot. Boat silence is required; confirm conversation-permitted areas. Swimsuit needed.

places.name: Cité Mémoire night walk
places.description: Local stories projected onto real buildings after dark. Try a couple on an evening walk.
places.note: Operator lists reopened scenes Wednesday–Sunday after nightfall. Check the current app map.

places.name: Ex-Voto
places.description: A well-curated mix of local clothing, ceramics, stationery, and home objects.
places.note: Pair with État de choc; both sit on the Saint-Laurent approach to Little Italy.

places.name: Bernie Beigne
places.description: Big, fluffy doughnuts and playful flavors. The fun sweet stop in this cluster.
places.note: Bernard Ouest. Check current hours and go before sell-outs.

places.name: Les chocolats de Chloé
places.mapQuery: Les chocolats de Chloé, 546 Avenue Duluth Est
places.description: Handmade chocolates, caramels, and crunchy chocolate-coated sponge toffee.
places.note: 546 Duluth Est; Saturday 11 AM–6 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: Monarque · Brasserie
places.description: The upgraded dinner pick: a handsome room, polished service, and ambitious French cooking.
places.note: Book the brasserie, not the separate four-course dining room. Saturday service from 5 PM.

places.name: Chez Potier
places.description: The refined pastry stop: individual cakes, chocolate work, macarons, and beautiful seasonal desserts.
places.note: 630 Wellington; Saturday and Sunday 8 AM–5 PM. Limited seating.

places.name: Bar George
places.description: Carved wood, stained glass, cocktails, and a grand mansion setting. Get a drink and the café gourmand.
places.note: The current menu lists five mini desserts for CAD 20. Bar seating is walk-in.

places.name: Ratafia
places.description: Inventive plated desserts with wine or cocktails. This is the dessert destination, not just a bakery stop.
places.note: Evening only, Tuesday–Saturday from 5 PM; closed Sunday. It replaces the evening plan, not a quick daytime detour.

places.name: État de choc
places.description: Bean-to-bar chocolates, tasting bars, and gifts that are actually worth bringing home.
places.note: 6466 Saint-Laurent; Saturday 10 AM–5 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

days.label: Friday night
days.title: Arrive, check in, get some poutine.
days.summary: Keep the first night easy. Park at the hotel and leave the car there for the weekend.

blocks.title: Check in at Le Germain
blocks.text: Drop your bags and settle in. Tell the hotel you will arrive late.

blocks.title: La Banquise
blocks.text: Take a taxi for a classic poutine. Share one if you only want a late snack, then head back to the hotel.

days.label: Saturday
days.title: Mile End → the river → a proper dinner.
days.summary: Mile End for shops, the Plateau for lunch and dessert, then the river and a better dinner.

blocks.title: Bagels and coffee in Mile End
blocks.text: Taxi to St-Viateur Bagel for a hot sesame bagel, then walk to Café Olimpico for coffee.

blocks.title: Browse Bernard, then visit LVNEA
blocks.text: Start at Bref for ceramics and design objects. Walk east to LVNEA and try a few locally made botanical perfumes.

nearby.text: Books and graphic novels on Bernard.
A wider selection of niche fragrances on Hutchison.

blocks.title: Lunch at Schwartz’s
blocks.text: Get a medium-fat smoked-meat sandwich, then walk toward Duluth for chocolates at Chloé. The nearby cards give you a pastry and pinball stop as well.

blocks.title: Bota Bota · the afternoon highlight
blocks.text: Reserve a two-hour water-circuit slot for hot-and-cold baths with river views. The boat is quiet; confirm where low-voice conversation is allowed. Bring swimwear.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel
blocks.text: Taxi back, warm up, and get ready for dinner.

blocks.title: Dinner at Monarque · Brasserie
blocks.text: Book the brasserie for a polished dinner with more room to choose your spend than the formal dining room. Save room for dessert. Allow CAD 85–130 each before tax and tip.

blocks.title: Bar George for a cocktail and mini desserts
blocks.text: Taxi to the mansion bar. Have one good cocktail and the café gourmand if you still want something sweet. Cloakroom is the nearby alternative.

days.label: Sunday
days.title: Old Montréal, chocolate, and a full afternoon.
days.summary: Keep the car at the hotel after checkout. Explore Old Montréal, then taxi north for chocolate and boutiques. Leave for Boston at 6 PM.

blocks.title: Check out, then coffee at Crew
blocks.text: Leave bags with the hotel and taxi to Crew Collective & Café. Have coffee and a pastry beneath the old bank ceiling.

blocks.title: Place d’Armes and the old streets
blocks.text: Walk to Notre-Dame’s square, then follow Saint-Paul east to L’Empreinte for Québec-made ceramics and craft. Continue to the waterfront for a short walk.

blocks.title: Chez Potier · pastries and a light lunch
blocks.text: Walk to the Wellington boutique for refined pastries and a light savory lunch. Pick up something for the drive as well. Olive et Gourmando is the nearby sandwich alternative.

blocks.title: Inside Notre-Dame
blocks.text: Return to Place d’Armes for the basilica interior. Sunday sightseeing opens at 12:30 PM and closes at 4 PM. Book daytime entry; this is separate from the evening AURA show.

blocks.title: Little Italy · chocolate and independent shops
blocks.text: Taxi to État de choc for bean-to-bar chocolate, then browse nearby Ex-Voto for design objects and small finds. Take this slowly and stop for coffee along Saint-Laurent. État de choc closes at 5 PM Sunday; Ratafia is closed, so keep its dessert bar as a Saturday alternative.

blocks.title: Collect bags and the car
blocks.text: Taxi back to Le Germain, collect your bags, and retrieve the car. Confirm parking and luggage storage after checkout. Pick up a takeaway meal before setting off.

blocks.title: Leave for Boston
blocks.text: Leave Montréal for Boston. Plan on a late-night arrival, around midnight or later with a meal stop, border processing, and traffic. Check live navigation and US-bound border waits before leaving; the earlier 10 PM arrival target no longer applies.

practical.title: Book the anchors
practical.text: Choose a hotel room with the right beds, reserve the afternoon activity, and book Monarque’s brasserie for Saturday 7 PM. Rates and live availability are not confirmed.

practical.title: Getting around
practical.text: Walk within each cluster. Use taxis between Mile End, the waterfront, and the downtown hotels. All food/activity amounts are planning allowances in CAD, generally before tax and tip; hotel cards link to live booking pages.

practical.title: The return drive
practical.text: Leave at 6 PM Sunday, with a late-night Boston arrival around midnight or later. Confirm live navigation, weather, and the US entry queue at Highgate Springs before departing. The earlier 10 PM arrival target is dropped.

neighborhoods.name: Mile End & Outremont
neighborhoods.subtitle: Coffee, independent design, perfume, and a polished bistro. Your Saturday morning cluster.

neighborhoods.name: The Plateau
neighborhoods.subtitle: Lunch, handmade chocolates, a great pastry, and a short game of pinball. Walk between these stops.

neighborhoods.name: Old Montréal & the river
neighborhoods.subtitle: The main afternoon and Sunday cluster. Chez Potier is at the western edge; Habitat 67 needs a taxi across the water.

neighborhoods.name: Golden Square Mile
neighborhoods.subtitle: Two polished evening stops near the downtown hotels. A taxi transfer from Old Montréal.

neighborhoods.name: Little Italy · the dessert detour
neighborhoods.subtitle: North of Mile End, so treat this as a separate cluster. Ratafia is an evening destination; chocolate and shopping work in the day.

hotels.name: Le Germain Montréal
hotels.label: Easy default
hotels.description: Refined, comfortable, and central. The cleanest shared-room choice.

hotels.name: Hôtel William Gray
hotels.label: Best old-city atmosphere
hotels.description: Stone architecture, contemporary rooms, and a real hotel living room. Best if you want the hotel to feel part of the trip.
hotels.beds: Confirm a two-bed category; many rooms are kings.

hotels.name: Le Mount Stephen
hotels.label: The grander option
hotels.description: A historic mansion paired with modern rooms, plus Bar George downstairs. The most overtly grand choice.
hotels.beds: Deluxe Two Queen Room is an official category.

hotels.name: Hôtel Nelligan
hotels.label: Warm, romantic old stone
hotels.description: Brick, beams, and a cozy Old Montréal base. A good counterpoint to the modern downtown hotels.
hotels.beds: Confirm the current two-bed room category directly.

headlines.label: My pick for a cold weekend
headlines.description: A two-hour floating-spa session. Book it, bring swimwear, and make this the afternoon’s one paid activity.

headlines.label: For architecture & design
headlines.description: Choose the 90-minute guided visit if Saturday tickets work. It replaces the spa, including its travel time.

headlines.label: The dramatic interior
headlines.description: Go inside Saturday while sightseeing is open. AURA is a separate evening ticket if you want a more produced light-and-sound experience.
